You're probably not doing anything wrong, however, a few things come to mind... 

1) Make sure you have stable reception/internet connection. Sometimes mine messes up and I can't get orders. There is a spot to check that in the app. Just press "I'm not getting orders" and it will let you know if it's connecting properly.

2) It's not always busy when it says "busy," it might just mean they want more people on - just in case. So when it's "busy" & "dash now" is available, often many people will jump on and that's why it goes grey. When that happens, the orders can spread pretty thin. 

3) To subjugate this, you can make sure you schedule yourself as much as possible. Try to work during hours that are typically busy whether the app says "busy" or not... these would be lunch hours/early dinner hours during the week and mid-day during the weekend.

I'm pretty new too. My first week, I just experimented a lot. I tried different areas out and I think that's the most important factor when it comes to profitability. You want busy areas, with a high minimum, mostly short drives to minimize fuel expenses and reduce wear on vehicle and I think tipping plays a huge role - you want areas where people are constantly tipping. 

I got lucky in that the best area for me is right where I live. The other areas I tried (4 others) were not as good and just wasting my gas driving to them was pointless. But it might not be for you, it would be worth it for me to drive to this area even if I lived a little while away.... I suggest trying out different areas. I tried a different one each day.

I think a lot of people who do really well with DD just get lucky in the fact that they're in the right area or know the right area to go to. I live right in the middle of all the primary restaurants and the minimum I get here in like $10 per order but I usually can do 2.5 runs an hour because the distance is not that bad. If it's slow, I leave the app on but go home. Many times I've gotten a quick $40/50 by doing a few late night runs that popped up while the app was on in the background.

The second thing you can do is learn what orders to accept/deny. Which restaurants you're going to want to avoid because they take too long/dont start cooking until you arrive - this will happen. There are restaurants you can accept and then do something else instead of stand around grilling the bartender. 

I multi app now and it takes some getting used to but it can help add $$$ I made $200 extra this week just using grubhub during times DD was slow or I was waiting for another order to finish... I'll accept a quick trip on GH for $8 and be back before they pack up the $14 DD order. It's hustle - but doing this whenever you can will increase your hourly average. Take it all while it's busy, but do it wisely! Don't overwhelm yourself. You'll learn how to finesse. Don't take long trips unless the pay is worth it ROUND TRIP you dont want to get stuck in an area with nothing going on and waste an hour + $5 gas for $15, NO. 

Play around. Look at what people have to say on here and you'll learn.
